w1.title: Worked Example 1: Scientific Definition of Work (W = F × s)
w1.question: A student lifts a 20 N water bucket vertically by 3 m. How much work is done?

steps.text: Identify upward force F = 20 N and vertical displacement s = 3 m.
Apply W = F × s since force and displacement are in the same direction.

check.q: If a person pushes a wall hard for 10 minutes but the wall does not move, how much scientific work is done?

opts.m: Without displacement (s = 0), scientific work W = F × 0 = 0.

w2.title: Worked Example 2: Kinetic Energy (½mv²) & Potential Energy (mgh)
w2.question: Find the potential energy of 10 kg of water stored 5 m high (take g = 10 m/s²).

steps.text: Given mass m = 10 kg, gravity g = 10 m/s², height h = 5 m.

check.q: If the speed of a moving bicycle doubles, its kinetic energy becomes:

opts.m: Kinetic energy is proportional to v², so doubling v gives 2² = 4.
Higher speed increases kinetic energy quadratically.

w3.title: Worked Example 3: Law of Conservation of Energy & Power (P = W/t)
w3.question: A solar water pump performs 1,200 J of work in 20 seconds. What is its power output?

steps.text: Given work W = 1,200 J and time t = 20 s.
Apply the power formula: P = W ÷ t.

check.q: What is the commercial unit of electrical energy used in household meters?

opts.m: Kilowatt is a unit of power, whereas kWh (power × time) measures energy.
Joule per second is a Watt (power).

NODES.title: Scientific Definition of Work (W = F × s)

steps.title: Scientific Definition of Work (W = F × s)
steps.body: Work is done when a force acts on an object and displaces it in the direction of the force: W = F × s (measured in Joules).

steps.title: Kinetic Energy (½mv²) & Potential Energy (mgh)
steps.body: Moving objects possess kinetic energy Ek = ½mv², while elevated water in an overhead Jal Seva tank stores gravitational potential energy Ep = mgh.

NODES.title: Law of Conservation of Energy & Power (P = W/t)

steps.title: Law of Conservation of Energy & Power (P = W/t)
steps.body: Energy can neither be created nor destroyed; it only transforms from one form to another. Power is the rate of doing work: P = W / t (in Watts).
